title: Valid Palindrome
description:
A phrase is a **palindrome** if, after converting all uppercase English letters into lowercase English letters and removing all non-alphanumeric characters, it reads the same forward and backward. Alphanumeric characters include ASCII letters (`'a'`–`'z'`, `'A'`–`'Z'`) and digits (`'0'`–`'9'`).

Given a string `s`, return `true` if it is a palindrome, or `false` otherwise. Note that if no alphanumeric characters remain after filtering, the resulting empty string is considered a valid palindrome.
constraints: s consists only of printable ASCII characters.
hints: You do not need to allocate a filtered copy of the string to check whether it is a palindrome.
Place two pointers at the start and end of `s`, skipping non-alphanumeric characters as they move inward.
Compare the lowercased characters at both pointers; if any pair differs, return false immediately.

examples.explanation: After filtering and lowercasing, the string becomes "amanaplanacanalpanama", which is a palindrome.
After filtering and lowercasing, the string becomes "raceacar", which is not a palindrome.
After removing non-alphanumeric characters, the string is empty (""), which reads the same forward and backward.
